record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: New Lyapunov functions for Volterra QSOs
record.original_question: Let S^{m-1} be the standard probability simplex and let a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on it be given by x'_k = x_k(1 + sum_i a_{ki} x_i), where A = (a_{ki}) is skew-symmetric and |a_{ki}| <= 1. For the dynamical system x^{(n+1)} = V(x^{(n)}), a Lyapunov function is a continuous function phi on the interior of the simplex such that lim_{n->infty} phi(x^{(n)}) exists for every initial point. Known Lyapunov-function families for Volterra QSOs include normalized monomials x_1^{p_1} ... x_m^{p_m}, certain coordinate sums under sign assumptions on A, and coordinate ratios x_i/x_j. Are there other kinds of Lyapunov functions for Volterra quadratic stochastic operators?

Theorem 1. [10],[14] For the Volterra QSO (7) the following assertions hold 1) For the dynamical system (7) there exists a Lyapunov function of the form ϕp (x) = x1p1 ...xpmm , where pi ≥ 0, m i=1 pi = 1 and x = (x1 , ..., xm ) ∈ intS m−1 .
2) If there is r ∈ {1, ..., m} such that aij < 0 (see (8)) for all i ∈ {1, ..., r}, j ∈ {r+1, ..., m} then ϕ(x) = m i=r+1 xi , x ∈ S m−1 is a Lyapunov function for QSO (7).
3) There are Lyapunov functions of the form ϕ(x) = xi/xj , i 6= j, x ∈ intS m−1 .
Problem 1. Does there exist another kind of Lyapunov function for QSO (7)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the standard probability simplex, and let $\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}$ denote its relative interior. A Volterra quadratic stochastic operator $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is defined by
$$(V(x))_k = x_k\Big(1+\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ki}x_i\Big),\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the matrix $A=(a_{ki})$ is skew-symmetric ($a_{ki}=-a_{ik}$) and satisfies $|a_{ki}|\le 1$ for all $i,k$. The discrete dynamical system generated by $V$ is $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$, $n\ge 0$, with initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$.

A continuous function $\varphi:\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a Lyapunov function for this dynamical system if $\lim_{n\to\infty}\varphi(x^{(n)})$ exists (in $\mathbb{R}$) for every initial point $x^{(0)}\in\mathrm{int}\,S^{m-1}$.

The following families of Lyapunov functions are already known for every Volterra QSO of the above type:
(i) Normalized monomials $\varphi_p(x)=x_1^{p_1}\cdots x_m^{p_m}$, where $p_i\ge 0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1$.
(ii) Coordinate sums $\varphi(x)=\sum_{i=r+1}^m x_i$, valid whenever there exists $r\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}$ such that $a_{ij}<0$ for all $i\in\{1,\dots,r\}$ and $j\in\{r+1,\dots,m\}$.
(iii) Coordinate ratios $\varphi(x)=x_i/x_j$ for $i\ne j$.

Problem: Determine whether there exist Lyapunov functions for Volterra quadratic stochastic operators essentially different from those in the families (i)–(iii) above, and exhibit such new families if they exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2019–2025) on Lotka–Volterra and Volterra quadratic stochastic operators continues to construct Lyapunov functions only for specific sub-classes (uniform Lotka–Volterra operators, ℓ-Volterra operators, infinite-dimensional sub-classes), rather than giving a general new family beyond the three known types. No source found resolves the general question of classifying or producing essentially new Lyapunov functions for arbitrary Volterra QSOs, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov functions and dynamics of infinite dimensional Volterra operators
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs Lyapunov functions for specific sub-classes of infinite-dimensional Volterra operators due to lack of compactness.
status_evidence.claim: New Lyapunov functions are only obtained for restricted sub-classes, not generally.

status_evidence.title: On Nonergodic Uniform Lotka–Volterra Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces uniform Lotka–Volterra operators and constructs corresponding Lyapunov functions.
status_evidence.claim: Progress is via special sub-classes, indicating the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Infinite Dimensional Lotka–Volterra Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dynamics with Lyapunov functions for specific subclasses in infinite dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: General classification of Lyapunov functions for Volterra QSOs is not provided.
